title: A model of human neural networks reveals NPTX2 pathology in ALS and FTLD.
authors: Hruska-Plochan, Marian; Wiersma, Vera I; Betz, Katharina M; Mallona, Izaskun; Ronchi, Silvia; Maniecka, Zuzanna; Hock, Eva-Maria; Tantardini, Elena; Laferriere, Florent; Sahadevan, Sonu; Hoop, Vanessa; Delvendahl, Igor; Perez-Berlanga, Manuela; Gatta, Beatrice; Panatta, Martina; van der Bourg, Alexander; Bohaciakova, Dasa; Sharma, Puneet; De Vos, Laura; Frontzek, Karl; Aguzzi, Adriano; Lashley, Tammaryn; Robinson, Mark D; Karayannis, Theofanis; Mueller, Martin; Hierlemann, Andreas; Polymenidou, Magdalini
one_liner_zh: 该文研究ALS/FTLD中TDP-43蛋白病理性聚集与NPTX2神经毒性通路，属神经退行性疾病机制研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Human cellular models of neurodegeneration require reproducibility and longevity, which is necessary for simulating age-dependent diseases. Such systems are particularly needed for TDP-43 proteinopathies(1), which involve human-specific mechanisms(2-5) that cannot be directly studied in animal models. Here, to explore the emergence and consequences of TDP-43 pathologies, we generated induced pluripotent stem cell-derived, colony morphology neural stem cells (iCoMoNSCs) via manual selection of neural precursors(6). Single-cell transcriptomics and comparison to independent neural stem cells(7) showed that iCoMoNSCs are uniquely homogenous and self-renewing. Differentiated iCoMoNSCs formed a self-organized multicellular system consisting of synaptically connected and electrophysiologically active neurons, which matured into long-lived functional networks (which we designate iNets). Neuronal and glial maturation in iNets was similar to that of cortical organoids(8). Overexpression of wild-type TDP-43 in a minority of neurons within iNets led to progressive fragmentation and aggregation of the protein, resulting in a partial loss of function and neurotoxicity. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed a novel set of misregulated RNA targets in TDP-43-overexpressing neurons and in patients with TDP-43 proteinopathies exhibiting a loss of nuclear TDP-43. The strongest misregulated target encoded the synaptic protein NPTX2, the levels of which are controlled by TDP-43 binding on its 3' untranslated region. When NPTX2 was overexpressed in iNets, it exhibited neurotoxicity, whereas correcting NPTX2 misregulation partially rescued neurons from TDP-43-induced neurodegeneration. Notably, NPTX2 was consistently misaccumulated in neurons from patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 pathology. Our work directly links TDP-43 misregulation and NPTX2 accumulation, thereby revealing a TDP-43-dependent pathway of neurotoxicity.
abstract_zh: 人类神经退行性疾病的细胞模型需要具备可重复性和长期稳定性，这对于模拟年龄相关疾病至关重要。此类系统尤其适用于TDP-43蛋白病(1)，该病涉及人类特异性机制(2-5)，无法在动物模型中直接研究。在此，为了探究TDP-43病理的发生及其后果，我们通过手动选择神经前体细胞(6)，生成了诱导多能干细胞来源的、集落形态神经干细胞（iCoMoNSCs）。单细胞转录组学及与独立神经干细胞(7)的比较表明，iCoMoNSCs具有独特的均质性和自我更新能力。分化后的iCoMoNSCs形成了一种自组织的多细胞系统，由突触连接且电生理活跃的神经元组成，这些神经元成熟为长寿的功能性网络（我们称之为iNets）。iNets中的神经元和胶质细胞成熟过程与皮层类器官(8)相似。在iNets中少数神经元内过表达野生型TDP-43，导致该蛋白的渐进性片段化和聚集，从而引起部分功能丧失和神经毒性。单细胞转录组学揭示，在TDP-43过表达神经元及表现出核TDP-43缺失的TDP-43蛋白病患者中，存在一组新的错误调控RNA靶点。其中错误调控最显著的靶点编码突触蛋白NPTX2，其水平受TDP-43在其3'非翻译区结合的控制。当NPTX2在iNets中过表达时，表现出神经毒性，而纠正NPTX2的错误调控则部分挽救了TDP-43诱导的神经元退行性变。值得注意的是，在肌萎缩侧索硬化症和额颞叶变性伴TDP-43病理的患者神经元中，NPTX2持续异常积累。我们的工作直接将TDP-43错误调控与NPTX2积累联系起来，从而揭示了一条TDP-43依赖的神经毒性通路。
